dial.summary: Five of eight macro indicators are supportive as the BTC Accumulation thesis holds: Global M2 continues its uptrend with US M2 at record $23.3T (+6.1% YoY), ISM Manufacturing holds at a 4-year high of 55.6% and ISM Services confirmed 54.1% (25th expansion month), the Fed balance sheet is stable at $6.74T, and BTC funding rates remain healthy near zero; DXY slipped to 99.66 on Iran diplomatic news that drove oil prices sharply lower, remaining in the neutral band; the 2s10s spread (now +0.39%) downgraded to neutral as the 30-day steepening compressed to +4bps (below threshold), with real yields the lone structural headwind at 2.47% though nominal yield declines on Aug 5–6 imply modest easing ahead; BTC at $64,580 with dominance at 56.64% and TOTAL crypto at $2.29T keep the BTC Accumulation thesis intact, with July NFP (Aug 7) and CPI (Aug 12) as the next regime-change catalysts.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) remains at $102.7T for June 2026, the most recent published global aggregate (central banks report M2 with ~30-day lag); July 2026 global aggregate not yet available; US M2 weekly (H.6 released July 28, 2026) shows $23.3T for the week of July 6—a record high, +6.11% YoY; the July 28 H.6 included a methodology update discontinuing the netting of IRA/Keogh balances as a direct component of M2, consistent with continued record highs; 4-week trend up: US M2 rising sequentially and global aggregate YoY growth rate stable at ~5–6%; status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; YoY contracting headwind condition not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released August 3, 2026 at 55.6%—2.3pp above June's 53.3%, beat 54.0% estimate, highest since May 2022 and seventh consecutive expansion month; companion ISM Services PMI July released August 5, 2026 at 54.1%—25th consecutive expansion month, slight miss vs 54.5% forecast; Manufacturing sub-indexes: Production 58.5% (+6.3pts, best since Nov 2021), Employment 52.8% (first factory expansion in 33 months), New Orders 56.7%; Services Business Activity 59.1% (+3.7pts), Services New Orders 57.2%, but Services Employment contracted to 47.4% (–3.8pts), tempering labor optimism ahead of July NFP (Aug 7); Prices Paid elevated in both (Manufacturing 71.1%, Services reversed above 70 for 4th time in 5 months); 4-week trend up: 53.3% (June) → 55.6% (July) = +2.3pp; status supportive (above 50 AND rising; headwind threshold of 62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.66 on August 6, 2026 (intraday, session range 99.65–99.90), down from 99.84 close on August 5; dollar weakened as oil prices tumbled on reports of an imminent US–Iran interim agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, reducing geopolitical inflation premium and easing rate-hike expectations; 30-day trend: ~101.34 (July 1) → 99.66 (Aug 6) = –1.7%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold, trend down; status NEUTRAL per ICE DXY spot threshold (at 99.66, above the 97.5 supportive boundary but below the 100 headwind boundary); July NFP (Aug 7, consensus ~85k) and CPI (Aug 12) are next directional catalysts—a soft NFP could push DXY toward 97.5 (supportive), while a strong jobs or hot inflation print could restore above 100 (headwind).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield) peaked at 2.47% on July 31, 2026 (FRED H.15); confirmed at 2.41% on July 29; nominal 10Y fell from 4.75% (July 31) to ~4.60% on Aug 5–6 driven by oil price collapse on Iran diplomatic news, implying real yields may have eased to ~2.30–2.40% in early August—specific DFII10 readings for Aug 5 unavailable due to FRED API access restrictions; value held at 2.47% (most recent verified peak); 4-week trend up: ~2.18% (July 2) → 2.47% (July 31) = +29bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold; September FOMC cut expectations constrained by ISM beat at 55.6%; July CPI Aug 12 is the primary real-yield compression catalyst; a sub-3% CPI print could push DFII10 below 2% toward neutral/supportive).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 6, 2026: DGS10 ~4.60% (declined from 4.63% on Aug 4 as oil prices fell on Iran diplomatic news), DGS2 ~4.21% (most recent confirmed Aug 4; 2Y likely eased marginally in parallel with 10Y); spread ~+0.39% (+39bps); 4-week comparison: July 2 spread ~+0.35% → Aug 6 ~+0.39% = +4bps, below the 5bps flat threshold—trend flat; status neutral (curve is positive at +39bps, consistent with growth expectations; however the steepening condition is not met on 30-day basis, removing supportive classification per scoring rules; headwind threshold of < –50bps not applicable; FOMC Minutes Aug 19 and September 15–16 meeting are next major curve catalysts; a sustained Sep cut-pricing driven steepening would restore supportive status).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL from H.4.1: most recent confirmed reading is $6,738,190M ($6.738T) for week ending July 29, 2026 (H.4.1 released July 30); search data also shows $6,735,609M as the latest indexed WALCL figure (representing a ~$2.6B decline from the prior week consistent with minimal ongoing QT); the H.4.1 for week ending August 5 released today (Thursday August 6) was not yet indexed in search at time of this run; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.72T (early July) → $6.74T (July 29) = +$0.02T (+0.27%), within the <0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (balance sheet holding at post-2022 plateau—$95B+ above one year ago; QT pace effectively minimal; no aggressive runoff with rising overnight rates).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: Live funding rate data inaccessible—CoinGlass returned HTTP 403; value carried forward at +0.004%/8h; contextual signals: BTC at $64,580 on August 6, 2026 (+~1.0% day-over-day), market cap ~$1.3T, BTC dominance 56.64%, total crypto market cap $2.29T; ISM Manufacturing 55.6% (4-year high) and ISM Services 54.1% (25th consecutive expansion month) confirm macro expansion consistent with spot accumulation rather than leveraged long speculation; funding rate well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold; 30-day trend down (from ~+0.006%/8h in late June to near-zero); status supportive (near-zero positive funding signals healthy long bias without leverage overheating).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $302B as of August 6, 2026 (USDT ~$188B, USDC ~$78B, balance in other stablecoins including USDS, DAI, PYUSD); total crypto market cap $2.29T; stablecoin dominance $302B / $2.29T ≈ 13.2%; 30-day trend down: July 6 dominance ~14.3% → Aug 6 ~13.2% = compression of ~1.1pp as capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets over 30 days; short-term note: dominance ticked up from the Aug 2 low of 12.6% to 13.2% as stablecoin market cap grew faster than TOTAL crypto over the past 4 days (new USDT/USDC issuance), but the 30-day direction remains down; status supportive (falling on 30-day basis; headwind threshold requires rising dominance WHILE TOTAL crypto is also rising—not met since dominance fell net over 30 days as TOTAL rose from ~$2.10T to $2.29T).

upcoming.title: CPI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—the most important inflation print ahead of the September 15–16 FOMC; arrives five days after July NFP (August 7); real yields at 2.47% (headwind) and DXY at 99.66 (neutral) make a soft CPI the primary catalyst for real-yield compression and a potential DXY break below 97.5 (which would flip DXY to supportive); ISM Prices Paid elevated in both Manufacturing (71.1%) and Services (reversed above 70 for 4th time in 5 months), signaling pipeline cost pressure; however oil prices fell sharply this week on Iran diplomatic news, which could provide a deflationary offset in the energy CPI component; June core PCE came in soft at 0.1% MoM, suggesting disinflation; a hot July CPI risks pushing DXY back above 100 (restoring headwind status) and is the principal near-term risk to the BTC Accumulation thesis.

upcoming.title: PPI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—released one day after July CPI (August 12); PPI feeds directly into core PCE components (healthcare and financial services); ISM Manufacturing Prices at 71.1% in July signals upstream pipeline pressure, but the sharp oil price decline this week (Iran news) could provide a significant deflationary offset to goods PPI; a soft PPI following a soft CPI would reinforce disinflation and support real yield compression from 2.47% heading into the September 15–16 FOMC; a hot PPI—especially in trade services or healthcare—would signal pipeline inflation risks not yet captured in headline CPI, complicating September cut pricing and potentially pushing DXY back above 100.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (July 2026)
upcoming.note: US Census Bureau Advance Monthly Retail Sales for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—key consumption gauge released alongside University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (10:00 AM ET); arrives one week after July NFP and two days after CPI, framing the growth-vs-inflation balance ahead of the September 15–16 FOMC; ISM Manufacturing at 55.6% (4-year high) with Production +6.3pts and Employment expanding for first time in 33 months suggests factory output is accelerating, which historically supports retail spending via the wage channel; ISM Services Business Activity also surged to 59.1%; a strong retail print (>0.4% MoM) would confirm demand-side support and reinforce the soft-landing narrative underlying the BTC Accumulation thesis.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (August 2026 preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment preliminary reading for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—released alongside July Retail Sales; July 2026 sentiment: 54.4 (beat estimate of 51.0, highest since February 2026); August preliminary is the first consumer confidence read post-ISM Manufacturing surge (55.6%), post-Iran diplomatic news and oil price drop, post-July NFP (Aug 7), and post-July CPI (Aug 12)—capturing near-term inflation expectations that directly influence September FOMC deliberations; the UMich 5-year inflation expectation component is particularly important given Prices Paid elevated in both ISM Manufacturing (71.1%) and Services (above 70); oil price decline this week may improve consumer confidence and reduce 1-year inflation expectations.
